title: Controlled Chaos: The Resonance
logline: Trapped inside a crystalline intelligence, Kirk must abandon force and trust Uhura's musical intuition and Spock's harmonic analysis to turn a cosmic cage into a conversation.

cast.name: James T. Kirk
cast.description: Original-series Captain Kirk, adult human man, short swept brown hair, gold Starfleet tunic, black trousers and boots. Decisive posture; moves from forceful intervention to trust.

cast.name: Spock
cast.description: Original-series Spock, adult Vulcan man, pointed ears, straight dark fringe, arched eyebrows, blue science tunic, black trousers. Restrained expressions and precise gestures; discovers the anomaly's harmonic structure.

cast.name: Nyota Uhura
cast.description: Original-series Uhura, adult Black human woman, dark upswept hair, red Starfleet uniform and communication earpiece. Alert, assured and expressive; recognizes that the anomaly is communicating.

visualStyle: Cinematic illustrated science-fiction fan film, original-series Star Trek production design, expressive readable faces, cobalt space and iridescent crystal light, controlled camera motion. Tell the story through actions and reactions; preserve the original song without added dialogue.
continuityRules: Keep the same three character designs, ages, hairstyles and uniform colors in every shot.
Use one consistent original-series Enterprise: saucer, engineering hull and two cylindrical nacelles; no later-series redesigns.
Maintain the same bridge layout and positions: Kirk at center, Spock at science, Uhura at communications.
The crystal signal begins irregular and threatening, then becomes synchronized and welcoming.
The crew solves the crisis through listening and cooperation. No unrelated battles, villains, cameos or extra crew close-ups.
No generated dialogue, lip-sync, subtitles, watermarks or logos. Any necessary titles are added in editing.

beats.title: The impossible signal
beats.goal: Establish the Enterprise, its crew and a repeating crystalline signal.

beats.title: The wrong answer
beats.goal: Kirk tries a conventional escape; show a clear consequence.

beats.title: Listen before acting
beats.goal: Uhura discovers intention in the apparent noise; Spock begins to translate it.

beats.title: A conversation
beats.goal: Build a joint solution: Uhura sends rhythm, Spock stabilizes the geometry.

beats.title: The quiet decision
beats.goal: At the musical breakdown, make Kirk's choice visible and legible.

beats.title: Controlled chaos
beats.goal: Pay off each character's contribution at the strongest musical section.

beats.title: An answered signal
beats.goal: Resolve the danger, reward the crew and return the opening motif with new meaning.

Cinematic illustrated science-fiction fan film, original-series Star Trek production design, expressive readable faces, cobalt space and iridescent crystal light, controlled camera motion. Tell the story through actions and reactions; preserve the original song without added dialogue.

Character continuity: James T. Kirk: Original-series Captain Kirk, adult human man, short swept brown hair, gold Starfleet tunic, black trousers and boots. Decisive posture; moves from forceful intervention to trust.
Spock: Original-series Spock, adult Vulcan man, pointed ears, straight dark fringe, arched eyebrows, blue science tunic, black trousers. Restrained expressions and precise gestures; discovers the anomaly's harmonic structure.
Nyota Uhura: Original-series Uhura, adult Black human woman, dark upswept hair, red Starfleet uniform and communication earpiece. Alert, assured and expressive; recognizes that the anomaly is communicating.

Current story beat: An answered signal. Resolve the danger, reward the crew and return the opening motif with new meaning.

Show this action only: The Enterprise emerges into open space; the crystal intelligence drifts freely behind it.

Wide cinematic exterior, slow tracking camera, clear ship silhouette and spatial geography.

Narrative consequence to communicate: The once-threatening rhythm becomes a peaceful farewell.

Keep the same three character designs, ages, hairstyles and uniform colors in every shot.

Use one consistent original-series Enterprise: saucer, engineering hull and two cylindrical nacelles; no later-series redesigns.

Maintain the same bridge layout and positions: Kirk at center, Spock at science, Uhura at communications.

The crystal signal begins irregular and threatening, then becomes synchronized and welcoming.

The crew solves the crisis through listening and cooperation. No unrelated battles, villains, cameos or extra crew close-ups.

No generated dialogue, lip-sync, subtitles, watermarks or logos. Any necessary titles are added in editing.

shots.consequence: The once-threatening rhythm becomes a peaceful farewell.
